message:
Good points all. Just to be clear, though, the "If you’re not going to teach a course exclusive of outside reading, why not use the most interesting reading there is?" part is not something I wrote; it's a quotation from Sirc. The way I read your post, it looks like that sentence is attributed to me. Or maybe you meant it as more like a Clancy-endorses-this statement, which is understandable. But I intended the quotation only to explain how my experience at UMN colors my reading of Sirc, especially the "writing studies" remark. It probably would have been better if I'd ended the quotation with the sentence preceding that question: "His is, indeed, writing worth studying."

I only espouse literature in the composition classroom insofar as I adhere to the "use all there is to use" idea.
